title: Combat tuning
description: Gameplay tuning owned by the Combat domain (Combat Bible). VeyraCombat binds it to FVeyraCombatTuning.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this file's format. A build reads exactly one version.

resistance.description: Armor and Magic Resistance mitigation (Combat Bible §3).

mitigationConstant.description: K in damage taken = raw × K / (K + resistance) for resistance ≥ 0 (Combat Bible §3). A larger K makes each point of Armor or Magic Resistance worth less.

targeting.description: Server checks of target validity and range (Combat Bible §30, §40).

serverRangeTolerance.description: Extra range in units the server allows on top of a cast range, measured edge to edge, for latency (Combat Bible §30: server range validation may include small latency tolerance). Provisional.

regeneration.description: Resource regeneration over time (Combat Bible §28: base resource regeneration continues in and out of combat).

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Canon gives no tick length, so it was drafted for playtesting.

tickSeconds.description: How often regeneration is applied, in seconds; each tick restores a unit's per-second rate times this. Shorter ticks fill bars more smoothly and replicate more often.

movement.description: Effective Movement Speed (Combat Bible §23, §39): the soft caps and the floor that ordinary slowing cannot go below.

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Combat Bible §49 lists them.

softCaps.description: Soft caps in rising order of "from". Speed above a cap's "from" keeps only "retained" of each extra unit, until the next cap. Empty means no soft caps.

from.description: The speed, in units per second, where this cap begins.

retained.description: The fraction of each unit of speed above "from" that is kept, above 0 and at most 1.

slowFloor.description: The lowest Movement Speed that slowing can bring a unit to, in units per second, unless its own base speed is lower. Stuns still stop it (Combat Bible §23).

forcedMovement.description: Displacement and dashes (Combat Bible §9, ADR-009 §2): each path is planned once, stopped by terrain and by the end of walkable ground, and its end moved to the nearest walkable point.

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Canon gives no number, so it was drafted for playtesting.

navigationExtent.description: How far, in units and in each direction, the end of a forced movement may be moved to reach walkable ground. With none that close, the unit stays where it is.

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Combat Bible §49 lists it.

tenacityFloorSeconds.description: The shortest duration Tenacity can shorten a crowd-control effect to, in seconds. An effect that starts shorter than this is not shortened.

combatState.description: Vanguard Combat State (Combat Bible §28): dealing or taking damage from an enemy Vanguard, or crowd-controlling or debuffing one, puts both in combat.

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Combat Bible §49 lists it.

outOfCombatSeconds.description: How long after its last Vanguard combat a unit leaves Combat State, in seconds.

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Combat Bible §49 lists it as a starting point.

assistWindowSeconds.description: How long damage, crowd control or a debuff on an enemy Vanguard counts toward an assist if it dies, in seconds.

killCredit.description: Who is credited with a kill the environment finishes (Combat Bible §18: an enemy Vanguard may still receive kill credit if they meaningfully contributed within the configured kill-credit window; otherwise the death is an Execution).

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Canon names the window but gives no length (ADR-011 §6).

windowSeconds.description: How recently an enemy Vanguard must have contributed to a death that something else finished to be credited with the kill, in seconds.

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Combat Bible §33 gives the prototype value.

effectiveness.description: Structure Effectiveness: the fraction of a basic attack's secondary riders (crit bonus, on-hit damage, empowered bonus damage) that applies to a structure. The attack's own damage stays at full effectiveness.

crit.description: Critical strikes on basic attacks (Combat Bible §5; ADR-022 §1).

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Combat Bible §5 gives the prototype values.

damage.description: Normal Crit Damage: what a crit multiplies the attack's base damage by, before Crit Damage bonuses.

chanceCap.description: The most effective Crit Chance, as a fraction; Crit Chance above it becomes Crit Damage.

overflowDamagePerChance.description: The Crit Damage each 1 of Crit Chance above the cap adds.

attackSpeed.description: Attack Speed limits and overflow (Combat Bible §22, §39): attacks per second stay between the minimum and the cap, and Attack Speed past the cap adds basic-attack damage on a curve.

provenance.description: Where these values come from (ADR-008 §7). Combat Bible §22 gives the formula and §49 lists the values.

cap.description: The normal maximum, in attacks per second, and the permanent reference that overflow is measured from.

minimum.description: The ordinary minimum, in attacks per second; below the cap.

overflowDamageScalePercent.description: S in overflow damage % = S × overflow / (C + overflow), where overflow is how far uncapped Attack Speed exceeds the cap, as a percentage of the cap.

overflowCurveConstant.description: C in the overflow formula: the overflow percentage at which the bonus reaches half of S.

pursuit.description: When a unit counts as moving toward an enemy Vanguard, for bonuses that hold only then, such as No Quarter's Movement Speed (Combat Bible §23; ADR-008 §9). Canon names the condition but not its limits.

range.description: How near, edge to edge, an enemy Vanguard the unit may acquire must be, in units.

maxAngleDegrees.description: How far either side of the unit's movement direction that Vanguard may lie, in degrees.

tethers.description: How the server keeps its tethers (Combat Bible §43; ADR-018).

checkSeconds.description: How often each tether's range, time and units are judged, in seconds.
